atoms.text: Road signs and traffic lights give all road users instructions on what to do. As a cyclist, it’s important to understand these. In the UK, we have four main types of road signs.

atoms.b: This is a warning sign, showing that there is a ((++zebra giraffe)) crossing. Warning signs are ((++red_triangles blue_circles)).
This is an information sign. This one shows that you can turn right to go to ((++Nottingham Manchester)). Information signs are ((++rectangular circular)).
This is a sign telling you what vehicles and cyclists must do. When cycling, you have to turn ((++left back)) here. Signs showing what you must do are ((red_rectangles ++blue_circles)).
This is a sign telling you what you must not do. ((++Cycling Running)) is not allowed here. These signs are ((++red_circles blue_squares)).

feedback.finish: The general rule is green means go and red means stop. You may also run into flashing red lights, which also mean that you must stop.

atoms.b: As a cyclist, you must also follow traffic lights. When the light is green, you can ((++go stop)).
When the light is amber, you should ((++stop jump)) behind the stop line unless you’ve already passed it.
When the light is red, you should ((++stop speed_up)) and wait behind the stop line.
When the lights are red and amber, you should ((++wait sleep)) and get ready for the ((++green blue)) light to show.
